prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the very near concrete pillar in frame 1 (roughly 0.2–0.5 m) from the bucket/pan and diagonal pole (about 0.5–1 m), with the ground, bamboo poles, and dark recess farther away (roughly 1–3 m). Across frames 2–5, the round bucket/pan remains low and near the camera, while the parallel bamboo poles extend upward and away; their gradual sideways shift mainly reflects the wearer turning or translating to the right. The hand/person fragment visible near the lower edge of frame 2 is within arm’s reach, but the map does not clearly separate it from adjacent surfaces, and no other complete person is visible. Depth makes near–far layering and partial occlusion by the pillar, bucket, and diagonal pole clearer than RGB, but the saturated white pillar, flattened dark background, inconsistent pole depths, and purely relative brightness make the metre estimates unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map marks only three regions, all concentrated in frame 1: a round left object mislabeled “donut,” the large central concrete pillar mislabeled “cake,” and a small lower-right region labeled “person.” It therefore gives coarse boundaries and shows that these regions are spatially separate, with the round object left of and below the pillar and the possible person region partly cut off near the frame boundary. It fails to identify the bucket/pan, bamboo poles, ground, diagonal pole, recess, and nearly everything in frames 2–5, so it cannot reliably support distances, facing direction, reach, occlusion, or motion across time. The masks make object extents easier to isolate than in RGB, but the implausible labels, missing instances, fragmented pillar mask, and absent later-frame masks make the result highly unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black in all five frames, so it detects no body or hand skeletons and provides no joints, orientations, facing directions, gaze cues, reach estimates, or person-to-object geometry. In the RGB strip, only a partial hand/person region appears near the lower edge around frame 2, partly occluded and cut off, which likely explains the failed pose detection. Because there are no tracked keypoints, the map cannot show whether anyone approaches, retreats, or turns across the sequence. It adds no spatial information beyond RGB and is unreliable here as evidence that no person or hand is present.
